name: Earlybird
identity_check: Confirmed as Earlybird Venture Capital (earlybird.com), the pan-European early-stage VC founded in Hamburg in 1997, now with offices in Berlin, London, Milan and Munich. Imprint names Earlybird GmbH & Co. KG, c/o Earlybird Venture Capital, Münzstraße 23, Berlin (HRA 60024 B, Amtsgericht Charlottenburg); managing directors include co-founders Hendrik Brandis and Christian Nagel. Fund lines found: early-stage Earlybird funds (Digital West VI/VII, Fund VIII), Earlybird Digital East (described by TechCrunch as associated with Earlybird but operating separately), Earlybird Health (health.earlybird.com, Berlin/Cologne), Growth Opportunity, UNI-X, Vision Lab and the E2D defence growth fund launched with AVP. Earlybird-X, its former pre-seed fund, has been renamed U2V and is now a separate firm. Not EarlyBirdCapital (the US investment bank) and not other firms with similar names.

thesis_text.value: Pan-European early-stage VC, founded in 1997, that backs tech founders from pre-seed to Series A with initial tickets of up to EUR 12M. Its current Fund VIII covers AI applications, software infrastructure and foundation models, and deep tech/hardware. Separate vehicles cover health, later-stage growth and, with AVP, defence growth, and it holds positions for the long term.

open_items: Fund close dates are the dates of the announcement or report, not legal close dates, except where a month is stated (Health I Aug 2018, Digital West VI Jul 2018, Digital West VII May 2022). The Earlybird IV month is the date of Unquote's report.

Earlybird funds I-III (1997-2009): no names, sizes or dates found. Digital East Fund I: the $150M size is from TechCrunch (2021), and the final close date is unknown. Its first close was $110M against a $130M target (GPCA, Jan 2014).

Growth Opportunity V: only the first close (June 2022, EUR 300m target) is documented, so the final size is unknown. Earlybird Growth Fund VI appears only as an SFDR disclosure dated 13 Oct 2026, with no size or close found.

E2D (with AVP): target €500m, with a first close planned for 30 June 2026. Earlybird and AVP act as advisors, with a dedicated team. Airbus Defence and Space was named anchor LP on 21 July 2026. Close amounts were not published.

UNI-X: only the €75M launch is documented (Tech.eu, Oct 2021), and no final close was found. Its team included Philipp Semmer and Michael Schmitt, who later led Earlybird-X/U2V. No size was found for Earlybird-X itself. U2V's €60M fund (Dec 2025) is not an Earlybird fund.
Vision Lab: fund size not stated. The program gives EUR 25K convertible loans to Germany-based pre-seed startups with at least one first-generation migrant founder.
The user list's 'AI apps and infra' and 'EUR 360M 2026 fund' leads are confirmed by the Fund VIII post. The $200M 2013-07 fund is the €150M 2013 fund (see conflicts).

No portfolio count is stated. The homepage shows 9 IPOs, 41 trade sales and 20 new investments last year, AUM €2.5B. About 119 company names are listed on earlybird.com/companies, but there is no total.

Nothing was found on investing in Indian founders, so that fact is omitted. Nothing was found on requiring a US entity either. Founders are invited to apply through the contact form, and no geographic rule is stated except that Vision Lab requires a Germany-based startup.

Rounds not recorded: Firstwork (Earlybird post, 21 Oct 2026) and Porters (11 Mar 2026). Neither Earlybird post gives the round size, lead or date, and no press page was fetched. SLNG ($3.9M pre-seed, led), TopK ($5.5M seed) and Brandback ($7.4M seed, led) appear in Earlybird's 2025 review without dates or co-investors.

Black Forest Labs: Earlybird says it made a follow-on investment in the combined Series A and B ($450M+), but the Series B coverage found (Dec 2025) does not name Earlybird, so the round is not recorded.

Aris Machina: the round date is only 'earlier this year' in Earlybird's Nov 2025 post, so the year is recorded. Sifted's article returned 403. Websites, HQ or founding years are not on the fetched pages for Bayshore, Avrea, SpAItial, Arago (HQ) and EthonAI (website/HQ).
Sifted and EU-Startups pages returned HTTP 403 and could not be read. Neuracore's EU-Startups headline gives €2.5M, which was not verified.

Roland Manger, who is quoted as Earlybird Co-Founder in the June 2026 E2D release, is not on the current team page, and his LinkedIn is not linked. The 2025 review names Ayush Jain as Partner, Growth Investments, but he is not on the team page either. Christian Nagel (Co-Founder and GP) is omitted because his stated focus is fintech, insurtech and foodtech.
Earlybird Health partners (Dr. Rabab Nasrallah and Dr. Christoph Massner, per the 2025 review) are not recorded because health is outside the target sectors.
